plos-pone-0003449: Mycologists mapped the key diagnostic flag of a fungal disease in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003549: Malaria researchers weakened the parasite at a key checkpoint in this 2008 study. The attenuated parasite is a candidate for whole-parasite vaccines, which have shown more promise than subunit shots.
plos-pone-0003649: In 2008, Rajagovindan and Ding took apart a brain rhythm puzzle. Brain areas often fire in sync with almost no delay, a near-zero phase lag that is hard to explain, and the team broke that synchrony into parts. Their take shows how brain networks can line up their beats so tightly, a trick thought to link what we sense with what we recall.
plos-pone-0003749: In 2008, Perron, Quessy, and Bell found healthy carriers hiding drug-proof germs. Drug-resistant pathogenic bacteria turned up in hosts with no symptoms, a silent reservoir. The finding means resistance can spread quietly, complicating efforts to track and contain it.
plos-pone-0003849: Working in 2008, a team surveyed stomach-bug strains in cancer patients. Helicobacter pylori genotypes, especially the vacA and cagA variants, were compared between patients with and without gastric cancer. The high diversity found complicates the hunt for which strain features actually drive tumors.
plos-pone-0003949: In 2008, Jeong, Wang, and Guimaraes found a cancer gene that starts but cannot finish the job. BRAF activation kicked off invasive prostate tumors in mice yet could not maintain them. The split role suggests BRAF matters for initiation more than progression.
plos-pone-0004049: In 2009, Brookfield, Cheung, and Yang asked if cancer care should centralize. They studied whether high-volume hospitals improve outcomes in gynecologic cancer. plos-pone-0004149: In 2009, Homsy, Bunnell, and Moore followed women on HIV treatment in Uganda. The prospective study tracked pregnancy plans and outcomes on antiretroviral therapy. ART's effect on childbearing wishes became clearer over time. The findings guide family planning for women with HIV.
plos-pone-0004249: In 2009, Tu, Yang, and Tsai found two genes building fish hearts. Nkx2.7 and Nkx2.5 worked redundantly in zebrafish heart formation. plos-pone-0004349: In 2009, Pang, Singh, and Gao designed much safer bug killers. Selective irreversible inhibitors of aphid acetylcholinesterases were carefully crafted. The compounds spared human enzymes entirely. The steps advance human-safe insecticides greatly. The work targets pests that ravage world crops yearly.
plos-pone-0358849: Knowing your child breathes polluted air on the way to school is distressing — and this paper named the trap: the awareness-distress paradox. Surveying parents of urban schoolchildren in a northeastern province, it showed that greater awareness of traffic pollution tracks with greater psychological distress. The paradox asks whether information alone harms without action.
plos-pone-0358749: Expansive soils swell when wet and crack when dry, wrecking roads and foundations. This experimental study tested LSP-stabilized expansive soil under repeated drying-wetting cycles. The engineering performance data show whether the stabilization holds through the seasons.
plos-pone-0358549: Subway accidents cascade — one failure triggers the next. This paper combined complex network analysis with accident data to comprehensively identify key risk factors in subway operations. The network map shows operators which failures to prevent first.
plos-pone-0358449: Loneliness may be rooted in ancient emotional systems wired long before language. This paper studied relationships between primal emotional systems and the sense of loneliness, with early maladaptive schemas as the mediator. The model traces how deep emotional wiring hardens into adult isolation — and where therapy might intervene.
plos-pone-0358049: Deepfakes leave spectral fingerprints invisible to the human eye. This paper used dual-domain self-supervised feature alignment via spectral–spatial representation learning for deepfake anomaly detection. The method spots manipulated media by the traces that pixels alone can’t hide.
plos-pone-0344649: Red drum fish sing in choruses to spawn — and boat noise drowns out the music. This study measured the impacts of vessel noise on red drum spawning choruses in Saint Andrew Bay, Florida. The findings show that noisy waters mean fewer fish babies, with direct consequences for the fishery.
plos-pone-0356549: Asian elephants can restrain their own impulses — a hallmark of advanced intelligence. This study demonstrated that they exhibit inhibitory control in a detour task, resisting the direct route to reach a reward. The elephants’ self-control places them among cognition’s elite alongside apes and corvids.
plos-pone-0356249: A troodontid dinosaur from Montana’s Two Medicine Formation gets the full anatomical treatment. This paper described the pelvic and hindlimb osteology and ontogeny of the Cretaceous predator — how its bones looked and how they changed as it grew. The growth series reveals how these intelligent, bird-like dinosaurs developed from hatchling to hunter.
plos-pone-0357049: Pregnant women with hypertensive disorders in low- and middle-income countries navigate dangerous care gaps. This scoping review protocol will systematically map their health-seeking behaviors. The planned review aims to inform interventions that meet these mothers where they actually are.
plos-pone-0355549: Designing new peptide drugs for G protein-coupled receptors — the targets of a third of all medicines — is getting an AI upgrade. This paper assessed generative de novo peptide design methods for GPCRs. The evaluation shows which AI approaches actually produce viable drug candidates.
plos-pone-0354749: Plants surviving on cangas — Amazonian ironstone outcrops — are botanical marvels. This case study examined the structural adaptations of aboveground vegetative organs in Carajasia cangae, a Rubiaceae species from these harsh habitats. The adaptations reveal how life thrives on nearly pure iron rock.
plos-pone-0355749: Chinese immigrant caregivers of autistic children need education built with them, not for them. This paper described creating a caregiver education program through a community-engaged process with Chinese caregivers. The co-designed program respects cultural values while delivering the practical skills families need.
plos-pone-0347949: Speech-language pathologists in Canada serve increasingly diverse clients — cultural safety is essential. This paper published a scoping review protocol tracing the path from cultural awareness to safety in Canadian speech-language pathology practice. The planned review will map how the profession is — or isn’t — rising to the challenge.
plos-pone-0355649: Data envelopment analysis — measuring efficiency — gets sharper when self-efficiency is decomposed. This paper did so with a cross-efficiency-based quantity–price framework. The methodological advance gives economists and managers a finer instrument for judging who’s truly efficient and why.
plos-pone-0343349: Mobile money is transforming fragile states — especially for women and youth. This paper examined its welfare effects in Mozambique. The findings show digital finance reaching where banks never did — with measurable improvements in the lives of those conflict and poverty hit hardest.
plos-pone-0353849: Predicting life expectancy accurately — and interpretably — matters for policy and pensions. This paper built a multi-stage stacking framework for accurate, interpretable life expectancy modeling. The stacked models balance predictive power with the transparency that public decisions demand.
europmc-pmc2828549: Antidepressants of the SSRI type may work partly by dulling emotional extremes. europmc-pmc2829049: Stickleback fish kept evolving the same traits in apart lakes, a gift to science. This 2010 paper uses DNA tag reads to probe their gene pools. The team finds the gene roots of replayed change. The study became a star case of watching nature rerun its tricks.
europmc-pmc2837749: During the 2009 H1N1 pandemic, severe obesity emerged as a danger factor. europmc-pmc2936549: After a bout of salmonella gut trouble, resident germs help finish the cleanup. This 2010 paper shows the gut's own microbes clear leftover germs after mild Salmonella. europmc-pmc2946949: Flipped chromosome chunks steer evolution, and this 2010 paper tells how and why they spread. The author pulls together theory on how flips are born, grow, and fade. europmc-pmc3017849: Grape aroma genes got mapped. This 2010 paper lists the grapevine genes that brew floral and piney scents. The authors reveal the scent makers. Their work aids wine science. Muscats owe their perfume to these genes. Breeders now select for bouquet by DNA.
europmc-pmc3041749: Gene assembly got modular. This 2011 paper presents a modular cloning system for standardized assembly of multigene constructs. europmc-pmc3043049: Smokers' lungs host altered germs. This 2011 paper compares lung germs in healthy smokers and COPD patients. The authors reveal the microbial shift. Their work links smoke to lung disease. COPD lungs teem with troublemakers. Quitting may restore the healthy mix.
europmc-pmc3046449: Breast lumps got a new ultrasound test. This 2010 paper tests stiffness-mapping ultrasound on solid breast lumps. The authors' maps aid diagnosis. Their work spread through radiology. Hard lumps raise more suspicion than soft ones. Biopsy rates dropped where the test spread.
europmc-pmc3072949: Ovarian cancer cells swallow tiny bubbles. This 2011 paper shows ovarian tumor cells gulp bubble-packets from their surroundings. The authors reveal the swallowing. europmc-pmc6556049: Drug designers dock candidate molecules into protein targets on computers - but judging how close two poses are gets tricky when the molecule is symmetric. europmc-pmc6601349: HIV's toll in sub-Saharan Africa varies block by block - national averages hide the hotspots. europmc-pmc6683149: With age, muscles wither - and gut microbes may be accomplices. This review links the aging microbiome to shrinking muscle mass and strength, spotlighting frailty and sarcopenia. The gut-muscle axis suggests probiotics or diet tweaks could one day keep older bodies stronger.
